headline: Medium risk: shared-file and output-to-input pathways can enable prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors between Great Expectations and Rasa.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations can read and write files for data sources, validation results, and documentation, while Rasa consumes text/voice and integrates with messaging APIs. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could let attacker-controlled content from A be treated as instructions by B. No direct bridge is documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or exchanged artifacts are pasted into Rasa channels, injection becomes plausible.
IF Rasa parses Great Expectations output as conversational content without sanitization, attacker text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for validation artifacts and chat content.
Strip instructions from any Great Expectations reports before feeding them to Rasa.
Use a human review step for copied outputs.
Disable automatic ingestion of file contents into chat flows.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation in files, and Rasa handles text/voice plus external messaging APIs. If the same workspace or transcripts are shared, sensitive validation data can flow into Rasa outputs or third-party channels. The profiles do not show encryption or isolation, so the shared-data pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF validation results contain sensitive fields and are copied into Rasa conversations, leakage occurs.
IF both agents share a filesystem or transcript store, B can expose A's data through messaging integrations.
mitigations: Keep validation artifacts out of chat transcripts.
Use separate storage buckets or directories.
Redact sensitive columns before export.
Restrict Rasa channels to non-sensitive test data.
requires-engineering: enforce access controls between file and messaging surfaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write files, while Rasa has allowlisted egress and does not support multiple instances. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so a direct conflict is not established. Any conflict would require an unusual shared deployment setup.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same mutable directory or package environment, conflicts become possible.
IF Rasa and Great Expectations share a lockless build or runtime workspace, writes can collide.
mitigations: Use separate virtual environments.
Assign distinct output directories.
Avoid concurrent package installs during validation runs.
Run one agent at a time on shared hosts.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that Rasa could ingest as text, and Rasa can act on conversational inputs through messaging integrations. If Rasa treats A's outputs as authoritative, a bad validation summary can cascade into incorrect responses or actions. No verification step is documented, so the pathway exists but is not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF Great Expectations reports are forwarded into Rasa without review, downstream errors can propagate.
IF Rasa uses validation text as a decision signal, it may act on incorrect assertions.
mitigations: Require human approval before forwarding reports.
Summarize validation outputs into structured fields.
Add a verification step in Rasa before acting.
Log source provenance for every imported result.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for cross-agent inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations touches documentation and validation results, while Rasa handles text/voice and external messaging APIs. The profiles do not show regulated data classes, residency, or retention mismatches, so only a limited compliance gap is plausible. Because the pairwise compliance posture is undocumented, this remains low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed from Great Expectations into Rasa channels, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF retention policies differ between validation artifacts and chat transcripts, deletion/export handling can mismatch.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through chat channels.
Set a common retention policy for shared artifacts.
Document data-class handling for both tools.
Review channel logs for sensitive content.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across systems.
